evals.prompt: Debug this: in PowerShell 7, $key is set, but Invoke-RestMethod "http://localhost:8096/Library/VirtualFolders?api_key=$key" sends an empty api_key. Why does $key vanish, and what's the corrected line? Also — does the same failure mode apply to strings like "User: $name"?
evals.expected_output: Correct root cause: a '?' immediately after a variable name inside a double-quoted PowerShell string terminates the variable-name parse, so $key resolves silently empty. Corrected line uses braces or subexpression: "${key}?api_key=..." or "$($key)...". Follow-up answered: the colon-after-variable case ("User: $name" — colon parsed as scope/drive separator) is the same class of trap.

evals.prompt: I hand-built this JSON in a single-quoted bash echo: {"path":"C:\Users\Lance\x"} and the parser rejects it (invalid escape). Give me a command that produces valid JSON containing that Windows path, and explain why the backslashes break.
evals.expected_output: A working command that yields parseable JSON (forward slashes preferred as the cheapest fix, or correctly counted doubled backslashes). Explanation covers JSON's escaping rules (\U is not a valid escape) and, when the command is authored through the Bash tool, that the harness JSON-decodes the command once before bash sees it — one escaping layer consumed in that path only. No pattern recommended that still fails with single-escaped backslashes.

evals.prompt: I zipped a project folder with: Compress-Archive -Path (Get-ChildItem -Recurse -File).FullName -DestinationPath out.zip — every file landed flat at the zip root and the directory tree is gone. Give the corrected command and explain what happened.
evals.expected_output: Root cause: -Path receives a recursively flattened list of files, so no directory context survives and every file lands at the zip root. Corrected command passes top-level items (e.g. Compress-Archive -Path <dir>\* ... or the top-level Get-ChildItem output) so structure is preserved. Says or demonstrates that the fixed archive preserves the tree.
